own_solution.law: Snell's law n1 sin(theta1) = n2 sin(theta2): sin(theta2) = sin(40 deg)/1.5 = 0.642788/1.5 = 0.428525
assumptions: ray in the plane of incidence; question refers to the final configuration

notes: Base: asin(0.428525) = 25.37 deg. With the incidence angle increased to 51 deg (T63FD, TB677): sin(51 deg) = 0.777146, /1.5 = 0.518097, asin = 31.20 deg. Going from rarer to denser medium, there is no total internal reflection at any angle, so no regime limit. T5D6B/TE795: the laser is tilted and returned, final incidence angle 40 + 11 - 11 = 40 deg, so the tilt cancels (it could also be read as D since it leaves no trace on the final geometry). The lamp sentences (TE869, T6C87) concern an unrelated light source: D. The numeric sentences all state 11 degrees consistently; T6C87 and T5D6B replace the number with 'a little', which I read as intended numeral-free versions.
